research_rationale:
basis_pattern: original_plus_bounded_search. EO 12261 (signed 1981-01-05; 46 FR 2023; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12261.txt, read in full) requires Federal agencies to use gasohol in gasohol-capable vehicles where available at reasonable prices and quantities, under section 271 of the Energy Security Act (42 U.S.C. 8871). Identity: the Title 3 heading of Executive Order 12261 of January 5, 1981, on gasohol in Federal motor vehicles, and the date agree with the register row. The dossier inventory held only subsection (b) of section 1-110, so I replaced it with eleven clauses (inventory override): the authority preamble and sections 1-101 to 1-110. Own terms: no section has an end date or ending condition; section 1-110 directs guidelines to be issued 'as they deem appropriate' and the held evidence does not show whether or when they were issued, so no performance end is claimed. Later instruments: a search of every held order text for the number 12261 finds only the order's own Federal Register copy, the 1989 codification snapshot, 42 U.S.C. 8871, 10 U.S.C. 2922c and unrelated page-number matches; the dossier chain lists EO 12716 and EO 12774 only because they amend or revoke Section 3-401 of Executive Order No. 12661 (National Commission on Superconductivity), which is not this order. The three selected machine searches were read with their coverage notes and record no revocation or supersession. Limit stated plainly: the continuing predicate rests on the held original text and the bounded searches; the U.S. Code edition runs through 2026-10-09 and the guidelines issued under section 1-110 are not held.

The held order texts contain no revocation, supersession or amendment of EO 12261; the dossier's two chain events (EO 12716 and EO 12774) concern Section 3-401 of Executive Order No. 12661 and are set aside as not this order. The catalog search records no disposition note.","independent_command_check":"Sections 1-101 to 1-110 are separate continuing commands, an exception, a delegation, a reporting duty and a definition; none was found ended, and the statutory authority they rest on (42 U.S.C. 8871) is still in the held U.S. Code text.","savings_check":"The order has no savings or transition clause and no ended clause, so no savings source other than the order itself is needed.","scope_check":"The corrected inventory has eleven clauses covering the whole order: the authority preamble and sections 1-101 to 1-110 (the two subsections of section 1-110 are kept together)."}
